image: Flag of the Province of Manitoba.svg
name: Manitoba
summary: A British red ensign with the Manitoba shield in the fly: a bison standing on a rock under the cross of St George.
origin: Following Ontario's example, Manitoba adopted a red ensign with its shield on 12 May 1966, the anniversary of the Manitoba Act of 1870, to retain a link with the Canadian Red Ensign.

symbols.name: Bison
symbols.description: An American bison standing on a rock.
symbols.meaning: The plains and the bison hunts central to Indigenous and Métis life.

facts: Its flag is nearly identical in layout to Ontario's.
The bison is Manitoba's provincial animal.
Proposals to change the flag to better represent Indigenous peoples have been made in recent years.
clues: A red ensign with a shield showing a bison on a rock.
Adopted in 1966, a year after a similar neighbouring flag.
Its animal is a symbol of the prairies.
